I1.quote: H2 chemisorption results showed that the H2 monolayer uptake volume of RuCMFN (80.76 µmoles g−1) was almost twice as that of RuCMF (44.93 µmoles g−1).

I2.quote: the Ru nanoparticles were nicely dispersed within the carbon framework of catalysts RuCMF and RuCMFN.
I2.location: main, p. 3 (journal p. 3760), Section 3.1 (Ru content 6.4 and 6.3 wt%, Table 1)

I3.quote: Searched the main text (Sections 2.3, 3.1, 3.2, Table 1, Figs 1-6) for the temperature and pressure of the H2 chemisorption uptake values (80.76 and 44.93 umol/g). Found only that the catalyst was 'cooled down to room temperature' before the H2 pulse (no number) and no pressure for the pulse. The 100 C and 8 MPa given belong to the D-glucose hydrogenation, not to an uptake measurement.

I5.quote: Ruthenium (Ru) nanoparticles dispersed in mesoporous carbon microfibers were prepared using alumina microfibers as the templates via a chemical vapour deposition (CVD) route.

notes: Catalysis paper (Ru in mesoporous carbon microfibers, D-glucose hydrogenation). Its only H2 uptake values are two H2 pulse-chemisorption monolayer uptakes (RuCMFN 80.76, RuCMF 44.93 umol/g; the text layer drops the mu, the page image shows umol). Method, main p. 2 (journal p. 3759), Section 2.3: 'A given pulse of hydrogen was then introduced from the built-in gas-sampling loop to the carrier gas, which passed through the catalyst bed. The total volume of hydrogen not adsorbed was measured using a thermal conductivity detector.' I read this as a measured H2 uptake by a flow (pulse) method, so I1 is met, but it is a borderline reading because it is a Ru-site titration for dispersion, not a storage measurement. If I1 were judged not met, the code would be the same (no_conditions_stated, the I1 fallback). I3 fails because the pulse pressure is never stated and the temperature is only 'room temperature'. No retraction (is_retracted false), not a review, no duplicate-data statement, text in English. No supplementary file supplied.
